Docs / Workflows

Ask ATL conversations and workspace access

Ask about a task

  1. Open a task and choose Ask ATL, or open the project conversation from navigation.
  2. Inspect the suggested focus and its evidence source. Use it as a starting hypothesis, not an established diagnosis.
  3. Choose discussion or fix mode and inspect provider readiness and context.
  4. Write the question. Use suggested question only fills the composer; it does not send.
  5. Send deliberately. A fix needs approval of the exact request and usable workspace access.
  6. Read the reply, inspect cited evidence, and retain the conversation. Completion still requires independent review and current checks.

If access fails, follow the recovery procedure below. Saving access or checking it does not automatically retry a provider request.

Ask ATL is available from a task's details or the project navigation. Each message has a Copy button; Copy conversation includes the stored messages. Copying preserves the original text and Markdown. Replies render paragraphs, lists, emphasis and code without allowing message HTML to execute.

Ask ATL now opens with a suggested focus based on recorded task state. It prioritizes unmet prerequisites, failed current-revision checks, recovery issues, exhausted session allowances and blockers. The project conversation points to a blocked task first. Use suggested question fills the composer without sending or approving a provider run. The suggestion names its evidence source and is a hypothesis: the provider must check it against current logs, recovery records and workspace evidence. Older conversation turns are shortened in the provider prompt to leave room for current evidence; the saved transcript and Copy conversation remain complete.

The composer stays below the scrolling conversation. New output follows the bottom until you scroll up. Jump to latest returns to new output. Provider activity and diagnostic disclosures retain their open state during polling. Drafts, provider choice and mode survive opening Workspace access and returning within the same page. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter requests sending; task fixes still use the existing exact-request approval and independent review gates.

Recover from an access failure

  1. In the conversation, choose Fix workspace access, or open Workspace access from the task's details.
  2. Select Read, edit and run commands in the task workspace, then choose Apply task access. Select Use project default to remove an override.
  3. Choose Check workspace access. On Windows this runs a local GapCode sandbox command which creates, reads and removes a unique temporary file in the task workspace. It uses no model session and no task-session budget.
  4. Return to the conversation and choose Prepare retry. Inspect the message and use Send message to review the normal approval request. Saving access and checking access do not automatically retry the failed provider request.

For a shared default, use Settings → Workspace access → Default workspace access → Save access default. This project setting applies to all models of the built-in GapCode and Codex CLI adapters, for Ask ATL and queue workers. Task overrides take precedence. Diagnose conversations remain read-only. Custom CLI adapters retain their own contracts; no machine-wide GapCode/Codex configuration is changed.

Settings are stored in config/manager.json:

{
  "execution_access": {
    "default": "workspace-write",
    "tasks": { "T-022": "workspace-write" }
  }
}

Only read-only and workspace-write are accepted. An absent setting retains the existing workspace-write default. Changes affect future runs and preserve task budgets, evidence, repair allowances and independent review gates. Browser mutations require the same owner session and CSRF protection as other Control Plane operations.

What the check proves

On Windows, GapCode now receives the named :workspace or :read-only permission profile and the existing unelevated Windows sandbox setting. Ask ATL previously passed only the legacy --sandbox workspace-write flag, unlike queue workers. Both launch paths now share one permission adapter; On Windows, both built-ins now receive the matching named permission profile: the codex executable may itself be GapCode's standalone alias. Non-Windows invocations keep the sandbox-mode flags. Before a real GapCode-backed fix, ATL runs a local read/write/remove sandbox probe before charging a model session. A failed probe returns its exact diagnostic. If a provider nevertheless starts read-only, ATL stops it immediately and preserves that failure category.

The October 29 T-023 incident reproduced this distinction: its codex alias started read-only with only --sandbox workspace-write, and started writable with the matching default_permissions=":workspace" and Windows profile. The local sandbox read/write/remove check passed for that selected executable.

Dependency readiness is separate. A task with dependencies needs its locked installation and matching .atl-dependencies.json receipt. Set workspaces.provisionLocal: true to authorize automatic offline npm ci with scripts disabled. The runtime uses its project-local npm cache and never downloads packages in that automatic route. If the cache is incomplete, it reports the exact npm error/package. A deliberate owner-authorized dependency installation can populate the cache; subsequent recovery verifies the receipt. Neither readiness nor unblocking proves an acceptance check or review passed.

A successful local check proves sandbox filesystem access. It does not grant approval to external MCP tools, override managed policy, verify a model's commands, approve work or complete a task. If filesystem access passes but a model's MCP tool still needs approval, inspect that tool's configuration and approval mechanism. The interface distinguishes this tool-policy failure from a provider account/model error. A zero exit with denied access is a failed fix, rather than work ready for review.

Browser tools for rendered checks

October 29, 2026 working-tree runtime: tasks whose objective, checks or skills require rendered inspection receive the atl_browser MCP server in Rowan, Sage and Beacon sessions. An integrated Beacon delivery also receives it. Task-scoped Ask ATL Fix uses the same tools. Diagnose remains read-only and does not start a browser. The built-in GapCode, Codex and Claude queue adapters attach session-local MCP configuration. Custom provider commands remain responsible for their own browser tooling; the runtime does not inject an incompatible MCP configuration into them or waive their evidence gates. No user-level provider configuration or approval policy is changed.

If the host rejects a call because its approval policy is never, use Task details → Browser access → Allow ATL test browser → Apply browser access. This authorizes the seven isolated preview tools for that task's future GapCode/Codex runs. The failure panel's Fix browser access button opens this control directly. Saving never starts a model run or unblocks the task automatically; review and send the next request separately.

For a shared default, use Settings → Browser access → Save browser default. Each task can Use project default, Require approval, or Allow ATL test browser. A task restriction takes precedence over an allowed project default. Check browser runtime starts and closes a disposable test browser without spending a model session or task budget. It verifies the runtime, not effective model-tool approval. Host-managed restrictions still take precedence; the Claude adapter retains its own permission handling.

The UI stores only this isolated-browser policy in config/manager.json:

{
  "ui_review": {
    "browser_access": {
      "default": "approval-required",
      "tasks": { "T-022": "approved" }
    }
  }
}

Choosing Use project default removes the task override. The legacy ui_review.local_browser_tools_approved flag remains a fallback when no UI default is saved. Other MCP tools, browser profiles and live task mutations retain their permissions. Browser changes require the existing owner session and CSRF protection. Task budgets, recovery history and evidence are preserved. Restart an older Control Plane server after updating its runtime.

The model starts browser_preview, reads browser_snapshot, interacts with browser_action, reads computed directions and isolation with browser_inspect, and calls browser_screenshot. The screenshot is returned as an image to the model and saved with UTF-8 DOM/style observations, viewport, locale, timestamps, asset hashes and a screenshot hash under the task's .atl-evidence/ui-review/. browser_viewport supports mobile checks and browser_reload refreshes repaired assets. Preview starts an isolated Playwright browser with disposable Control Plane fixture state; it does not use the user's Chrome profile or expose live manager mutations. Navigation and browser requests are restricted to the fixture origin and GET/HEAD. This initial adapter covers ATL Control Plane assets, not arbitrary websites.

Playwright must resolve from the project or task workspace. ATL prefers its installed Chromium; ATL_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE can select an existing browser binary. Missing dependencies are reported before a worker session starts; an executable path alone does not establish a working browser connection. browser_preview establishes that connection. A host denial remains an environment blocker, not permission to relax policy or claim a PASS.

Capture receipts deliberately say NOT OBSERVED. The model must examine the image, compare the requested behavior, and submit its exact check and current source revision through the existing scoped observe command. Capturing an image never completes a task or replaces independent review. A local T-022 rendering check can precede T-024's integrated review.

Regression verification: node verification/ui_review_mcp_test.mjs exercises the actual stdio handshake, provider argument injection, browser startup, Persian fixture, image return, evidence artifacts and shutdown. It verifies tool transport, not a model's visual judgment or T-022 completion.

An October 29 real Ask ATL smoke session without browser authorization was denied by the host's never policy. A second isolated smoke project enabled only its task's browser permission. GapCode / gpt-6-luna then called preview, snapshot, action, inspection and screenshot tools; received and inspected the returned image; and reported the Persian sentence as RTL with its Latin path LTR and isolated. The transcript and screenshot are under .trust/browser-tool-smoke-1793253400838/. This proves the model-to-browser path in that environment. It does not complete T-022 or replace its review; the live project's permissions and task state were not changed.

verification/browser_access_test.mjs verifies project/task inheritance, the exact per-tool provider arguments, owner/CSRF enforcement, snapshots, legacy compatibility and preserved budgets/state. The desktop/mobile path through task settings, project defaults and the failure shortcut is covered by verification/control_plane_modal_test.mjs. These checks are included in the runtime CI workflow; remote CI has not been observed for this change.

October 28, 2026 observation

T-022's saved failed fix used gapgpt / gpt-6-luna. Its diagnostic reported command-policy denials and an MCP call requiring approval while the nested session's approval policy was never. The earlier instruction to choose a different provider conflated filesystem access with tool execution policy.

After unifying the profile arguments, a real GapCode sandbox check inside T-022's workspace passed read/write/readback/cleanup. No additional model run or task session was used. A model-driven repair and independent T-022 review remain separate, unobserved gates for this change.

Contract Evidence Scope / remaining uncertainty
Project default and task overrides verification/execution_access_test.mjs Inheritance, validation, model-independent arguments, owner/CSRF rejection and budget preservation
Assistant/queue launch compatibility Access, assistant and worker regression checks Shared permission arguments; custom CLIs keep their own policy
Generated stylesheet npm run ui:css:check SCSS matches shipped HTML
Sandbox filesystem access Local GapCode probe in T-022 Passed; external MCP approval is separate
Conversation interface Chrome desktop and narrow-screen inspection Copy reply/error, draft return, disclosure state, composer visibility and no modal horizontal overflow observed
Model-driven repair and overnight completion Not observed No claim of completed T-022 review or successful unattended overnight run

To roll back the settings, remove task overrides with Use project default or select the prior project default. This does not restore consumed sessions or erase failure history. Use the current project server for these endpoints; restart an older Control Plane server after updating its runtime.
